refuted.fact: Fact 35, cited to https://astral.sh/pyx: "The page gives no date for this change and no reason, and does not mention OpenAI."
refuted.why: REFUTED on the "does not mention OpenAI" clause. I fetched https://astral.sh/pyx myself (HTTP 200, 38,110 bytes) and it contains 2 case-insensitive occurrences of "OpenAI": Astral runs a site-wide announcement bar at the top of the page reading Astral to join OpenAI as part of the Codex team →, wrapped in a link. The same bar is on https://astral.sh/ (200, 144,076 bytes). The rest of fact 35 is confirmed verbatim: "pyx is no longer accepting new signups.", "A Python-native package registry from the creators of uv.", customers Ramp / Intercom / fal, and indeed no date and no reason for the signup closure.

unsupported.fact: Fact 37: "OpenAI's Codex developer documentation landing page, fetched 2026-09-16, contains zero occurrences of 'astral', 'ruff' or 'uv'. Six months after the announcement, OpenAI's public Codex docs do not surface the Astral tools." — cited to https://developers.openai.com/codex/
unsupported.why: UNSUPPORTED AS CITED. That URL serves no page: curl -A Mokaair-editorial returns HTTP 308 to /codex, which returns HTTP 308 to https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs — a different host. The 200 that comes back is the ChatGPT Learn docs shell; its extracted visible text (12,413 chars) is a navigation index, and it contains zero occurrences of "python" as well, which shows the zero counts are an artefact of a nav shell rather than evidence about Codex documentation. The researcher recorded a URL it never landed on and built a negative-evidence claim on a page that could not carry that evidence. A correctly sourced replacement exists: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt (200, 1,809,784 bytes, "# Codex — full documentation / > Single-file Markdown export of ChatGPT docs for Codex across the CLI, IDE, cloud, and SDK.") has zero occurrences of astral / ruff / uv, as does https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms.txt (200, 26,062 bytes).

additional_findings: BETTER FIRST-PARTY SOURCE for fact 37: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt (200, 1,809,784 bytes) is OpenAI's own single-file Codex documentation export and has ZERO case-insensitive hits for astral, ruff or uv; the curated index https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms.txt (200, 26,062 bytes) is likewise zero. Attach that URL, not developers.openai.com/codex/. Even then it is weak negative evidence and must be written as 「OpenAI 的 Codex 文件未提到」, never as a statement about OpenAI's intentions.

MATERIAL OMISSION that weakens fact 19: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ carries a git-revision footer with title="March 13, 2026 14:17:06 UTC". That index page has not been revised since six days BEFORE the 2026-03-19 announcement, so "the uv docs still say backed by Astral" is not evidence of any post-deal decision. https://docs.astral.sh/ty/ does carry September 15, 2026 (researcher correct). https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/ carries no revision date at all, which the researcher did not say.

MATERIAL OMISSION in fact 34: Astral's own footnote qualifies the 4x-10x uv audit figure — "Comparisons between uv audit and pip-audit are slightly apples-to-oranges, since the representative uses of the two are often different. The short version: uv audit is significantly faster than most equivalent pip-audit invocations, but using pip-audit with a fully-primed cache can be roughly as fast as uv audit." If the article uses 4x-10x at all it must carry this qualifier.

MISSING SIX-MONTHS-LATER EVIDENCE that is stronger and safer than the developers.openai.com claim: https://astral.sh/about (200, 79,571 bytes, checked 2026-09-16) still bylines Charlie Marsh as "Founder, Astral", still says "We're growing the team / Not rapidly, but deliberately" and "We're a small, distributed team of software engineers", and states "We build in the open. Our tools are open source and permissively licensed." No statement of OpenAI ownership anywhere on it. (It lists only Ruff and uv in the mission section, not ty.)

MISSING FIRST-PARTY CONTEXT: six months on, Astral itself is still surfacing the deal via the site-wide banner "Astral to join OpenAI as part of the Codex team →" on astral.sh pages. This is a usable fact and it is the direct counter-evidence to fact 35.

LIVE-FEED DRIFT (do not copy the number into the article): facts 4 and 38 say "1,194 items". My fetch of https://openai.com/news/rss.xml today returned 1,195 <item> elements (726,611 bytes, newest pubDate 2026-09-16 16:00:00 UTC, oldest 2015-12-11). The substance holds — exactly one item matches "astral" and it is the 2026-03-19 announcement, verbatim as quoted (title "OpenAI to acquire Astral", description "Accelerates Codex growth to power the next generation of Python developer tools", category "Company", link https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-astral). A rolling count must not appear in the article.

OBSERVATION, do NOT write as fact: OpenAI's feed distinguishes "OpenAI to acquire X" (Astral 2026-03-19, Ona 2026-06-11, Promptfoo 2026-03-09, Neptune 2025-12-03) from "OpenAI acquires X" (TBPN 2026-04-02, Rockset 2024-06-21, Global Illumination 2023-08-16). The Astral headline uses the pending form, which supports the researcher's "agreed but not closed" reading. It is a pattern, not a stated rule, so it cannot be presented as something OpenAI said.

SOURCE-SLOT COMPLIANCE, needs an editor decision rather than a silent fix: BRIEF.md says 「sources 放的是文章頁的網址，不是 feed 的網址」, and source slot 2 is a feed. I independently reproduced the block that justifies it: https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-astral 403 (9,791 bytes), trailing-slash form 403, /ja-JP/ 403, /zh-Hant/ 403, .md variants 403, https://openai.com/ itself 403. The feed genuinely is the only reachable OpenAI-authored text about the deal, and the researcher disclosed the exception explicitly, which is the right handling.

PATH-CONSTRUCTION NOTE, no fabrication found: facts 26-29 use raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/<repo>/main/<file> paths that are conventional rather than linked from any page the researcher read. I fetched all five and each returned 200 with exactly the claimed content (uv LICENSE-MIT "Copyright (c) 2025 Astral Software Inc.", uv LICENSE-APACHE Apache 2.0, ruff LICENSE "Copyright (c) 2022 Charles Marsh", ty LICENSE "Copyright (c) 2025 Astral Software Inc."), so nothing is invented — but the record should have said these paths were constructed.

CHANGELOG SCOPE CAVEAT for fact 29: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/uv/main/CHANGELOG.md (50,166 bytes) holds only the 0.12 series in full — 16 headings 0.12.0 to 0.12.15, "Released on 2026-07-28" through "Released on 2026-09-15" (0.12.14 and 0.12.15 share 2026-09-15) — with 0.11.x and older as pointers. So it evidences continuous releases from 2026-07-28 onward, not across the whole 2026-03-19 to 2026-09-15 window. The 16-release count and both dates are exact.
NO DISQUALIFYING SOURCE FOUND: none of the 38 facts traces to a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet. pypi.org is the PSF's official index and is first-party for package metadata.

NO DATE CONFLATION FOUND: event_date 2026-03-19 is carried by two independent first-party channels (Astral MDX frontmatter "date":"2026-03-19" plus rendered "March 19, 2026"; OpenAI feed pubDate "Thu, 19 Mar 2026 00:00:00 GMT" — and 2026-03-19 is a Thursday). The researcher correctly refuses to treat the sitemap <lastmod>2026-08-31T19:59:25.765Z</lastmod> as a deal date; I re-fetched https://openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ (200, 261 <url> entries) and that lastmod is exact, with 65 hreflang alternates including zh-Hant, zh-Hans-CN, ja-JP and ko-KR ("roughly sixty" is fair).

VENDOR-CLAIM HANDLING IS CORRECT: the "hundreds of millions of downloads per month" figure, the Codex-integration intention, the open-source commitment and the 4x-10x audit figure are all flagged is_vendor_claim true. I found no vendor claim recorded as independent fact. Note the announcement's open-source commitment reaches the reader only through Astral's words — the researcher flags this correctly and the writer must keep it that way, because OpenAI's own page was never read.

SPOT-CHECKS THAT CAME BACK EXACT, for the writer's confidence: Ruff v0.16.0 post (frontmatter 2026-07-23, Brent Westbrook) says verbatim "Ruff now enables 413 rules by default, up from 59 in previous versions. Since Ruff's default rule set was last modified in v0.1.0, the number of rules in Ruff has grown from 708 to 968" and lists exactly the 18 removed rules E401, E402, E701, E702, E703, E711, E712, E713, E714, E721, E731, E741, E742, E743, F403, F405, F406, F722. PyPI JSON: uv 0.12.15 uploaded 2026-09-15T12:07:02Z, license_expression "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; ruff 0.16.7 uploaded 2026-09-10T18:03:30Z, "MIT"; ty 0.0.81 uploaded 2026-09-15T02:04:51Z, license_expression null. The 2023 launch post (frontmatter 2023-04-18) says "We’ve raised $4m in seed funding led by Accel, with participation from Caffeinated Capital, Guillermo Rauch (Vercel), Solomon Hykes (Docker), David Cramer (Sentry), and others." All of the announcement's outbound links are as described, including "OpenAI's own announcement" -> https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-astral/ and Codex -> https://chatgpt.com/codex.
